Samira — thanks for the diagram. I pushed a small revision (v0.9) and an outline runbook draft to address the items you called out. High-level answers up front: 

- Control plane egress: we strongly prefer a dedicated egress path for control traffic (separate NAT/gateway) to avoid noisy-tenant interference. That lets us enforce QoS and rate-limits from our side. If you must NAT through primary edge, we can support it, but we need a stable 1:1 public IP and consistent ACLs.

- KV cache persistence: in the current design KV cache is in-memory on the inference nodes with optional periodic snapshots to the internal object store (S3-compatible). During a rolling upgrade we rely on in-memory warmup + prefix cache warmers; snapshots are a best-effort restoration. We documented the expected warm-up window (~60-120s per pod) in the runbook.

- Routing: Redwood's recommended pattern is BGP for cross-rack failover in colo; we will advertise /32s for control plane endpoints and prefer BGP with graceful restart support. Static routes are acceptable for smaller single-rack deployments but complicate automated failover.

I called out two items that will need changes on your side before cutover:
1) Reserve an extra /29 for control-plane NAT addresses (we list exact IPs in v0.9).
2) Allow outbound 443 to our controller endpoints on the listed FQDNs and a short list of telemetry ports.

I pulled the runbook into the Drive link and attached a PDF snippet. Can Kimberly and Irene scan the runbook for operational gaps? I'll incorporate feedback and then propose a concrete cutover plan.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
(Attachment: pre-cutover-runbook-draft.md)
